claims.text: The identity of X in CrFeCoNiX governs whether a protective oxide scale forms and persists above 900 °C.
Si promotes selective formation of a continuous silica-rich SiO2 scale.
The SiO2 scale is viscous and adherent.
A silica-rich scale suppresses further oxidation and resists spallation.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX forms less coherent oxide scales that tend to crack or spall under thermal stress.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX forms less coherent oxide scales that tend to crack or spall under thermal stress.
Al in an Al-containing Fe-Ni-Co-Cr alloy can oxidize to form an Al2O3-containing oxide.
Low oxygen diffusivity and high viscosity of SiO2 create a coherent barrier that limits oxygen ingress.
The SiO2 barrier limits thermal stresses in the oxide scale.
Mn- and Al-based scales have faster diffusion rates than the proposed SiO2 scale.
Mn- and Al-based scales undergo volume changes and have poorer adhesion, making them more prone to cracking.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative conditions, the Si-containing alloy will retain a more continuous, adherent, and less cracked scale than the Mn-containing alloy.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative conditions, the Si-containing alloy will retain a more continuous, adherent, and less cracked scale than the Al-containing alloy.
Substantial secondary-phase segregation or processing-induced defects may alter oxidation kinetics and invalidate the proposed comparison.
Grain size and trace impurities may influence oxide thickness, cracking, and protection.
The proposed test compares Si-, Mn-, and Al-containing variants at 950 °C after nominally identical fabrication and exposure.
Failure of the Si-containing alloy to show a more continuous, adherent, and less cracked scale than both comparators would falsify the hypothesis.
